--- title: "Week 17" author: "Victoria Sjalim" date: "2026-11-16" format: html execute: freeze: auto --- # Comparison between the variant and collapse modes ::: {#803fdd57 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd import matrix as mt RESULTS = {"collapse": "../result/eris_validation", "variant": "../result/eris_validation_variant"} ASSEMBLIES = {"complete": "Complete genome (FASTA)", "simulated": "Simulated GFA", "real": "Real-reads GFA"} TRUTH = {"complete": mt.GT_COMPLETE, "simulated": mt.GT_CHROMOSOME, "real": mt.GT_COMPLETE} def read_loci(report): """One row per IS name: its copies, from the number of loci (variant) or their copy_number (collapse).""" loci = pd.read_csv(report, sep="\t").drop_duplicates("locus_id") loci["copies"] = loci["copy_number"].fillna(1) if "copy_number" in loci else 1 loci = loci.assign(target=loci["target"].str.split(",")).explode("target") # a locus can hold several IS loci["name"] = loci["target"].map(mt.is_name) by_name = loci.groupby("name")["copies"].sum().reset_index() by_name["group"] = by_name["name"].map(mt.is_group) return by_name metrics = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f"{path}/metrics.tsv", sep="\t").assign(mode=mode) for mode, path in RESULTS.items()]) side = metrics[(metrics["dimension"] == "side") & (metrics["class"] == "both")] relations = side.set_index(["assembly_type", "mode"])[["TP", "FN", "TP_calls", "FP", "precision", "recall", "f1"]] loci = pd.DataFrame([{"assembly_type": a, "mode": mode, **mt.precision_recall_gfa(mt.read_truth(bed, exclude=["ISSen10"]), read_loci(f"{path}/EC958/{a}/eris/h3_report.tsv"))[0]} for a, bed in TRUTH.items() for mode, path in RESULTS.items()]) loci = loci.set_index(["assembly_type", "mode"])[["TP", "FN", "FP", "precision", "recall", "f1"]] table = pd.concat({"IS–CDS relations": relations, "IS loci": loci}, axis=1).round(2) table = table.reindex(list(ASSEMBLIES), level=0).rename(index=ASSEMBLIES) table.index.names = ["assembly", "mode"] table ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

Every FN also has a miss cause (`budget`, `not_reported`, `not_called`). ::: {#365a7b24 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} rows = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f"{path}/EC958/{a}/relations.tsv", sep="\t").assign(assembly=name, mode=mode) for mode, path in RESULTS.items() for a, name in ASSEMBLIES.items()], ignore_index=True) rows["reason"] = rows["reason"].fillna("–") columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([list(ASSEMBLIES.values()), list(RESULTS)]) pd.crosstab([rows["status"], rows["reason"]], [rows["assembly"], rows["mode"]]).reindex(columns=columns, fill_value=0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: - Variant mode reports every path through a collapsed repeat, not one consensus per repeat - **Higher recall**: a copy whose flanks collapse mode left out can still appear as a variant path. Every TP variant mode gains was a `not_reported` miss in collapse mode: 12 on simulated and 18 on real. They’re mostly multi-copy IS such as ISEc12 (4 and 5), IS26, ISEc23, IS200 and ISEc52. - **Lower precision**: the graph allows combinations that don’t exist in the genome. Each of those paths becomes a locus, and its nearest genes become FP calls. That’s why the extra FPs are almost all not_in_truth (29 → 44 on real) and come from multi-copy IS: ISEc8 (+3), IS30 (+3), ISEc23, ISEc12, IS1A and IS3411 (+2 each). - Precision counts each call: one extra path through a repeat adds two new nearest-flank calls, one per side. So every wrong path costs precision twice. # Comparing pyfgs and real FGS - I run FGS only in complete genome and found there are 5620 genes that are similar between pyfgs, genome FragGeneScan 1.32 was run on the complete genome outside eris, with the `complete` model in both its modes: `-w 0` (fragments, what eris uses: `GeneFinder(model=Model.Complete, whole_genome=False)`) and `-w 1` (whole genome). Genes are compared by replicon, start, end and strand. ::: {#b4b7ad2f .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} def read_genes(gff): genes = pd.read_csv(gff, sep="\t", comment="#", header=None, usecols=[0, 2, 3, 4, 6], names=["replicon", "type", "start", "end", "strand"]) genes = genes[genes["type"] == "CDS"] return set(genes[["replicon", "start", "end", "strand"]].itertuples(index=False, name=None)) GENE_CALLS = {"pyfgs (eris, w0)": "../result/eris_validation/EC958/complete/eris/h3_assembly.gff", "FGS 1.32 w0": "../result/fraggenescan_complete/EC958_fgs_w0.gff", "FGS 1.32 w1": "../result/fraggenescan_complete/EC958_fgs.gff"} calls = {name: read_genes(path) for name, path in GENE_CALLS.items()} REPLICONS = {"HG941718.1": "chromosome", "HG941719.1": "pEC958", "HG941720.1": "pEC958B"} pd.DataFrame({name: {"genes": len(g), **{label: sum(x[0] == r for x in g) for r, label in REPLICONS.items()}} for name, g in calls.items()}).T ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {#d5e182d5 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} def stop(gene): replicon, start, end, strand = gene return replicon, end if strand == "+" else start, strand names = list(calls) pd.DataFrame([{"first": a, "second": b, "identical": len(calls[a] & calls[b]), "same stop": len({stop(g) for g in calls[a]} & {stop(g) for g in calls[b]}), "only first (by stop)": len({stop(g) for g in calls[a]} - {stop(g) for g in calls[b]}), "only second (by stop)": len({stop(g) for g in calls[b]} - {stop(g) for g in calls[a]})} for i, a in enumerate(names) for b in names[i + 1:]]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

0 pyfgs (eris, w0) FGS 1.32 w0 5620 5620 5 49
1 pyfgs (eris, w0) FGS 1.32 w1 4262 5142 483 95
2 FGS 1.32 w0 FGS 1.32 w1 4262 5146 523 91
``` ::: ::: - With the same setting (`-w 0`), pyfgs and FragGeneScan agree on 5,620 genes exactly. pyfgs alone has 5 genes, all 66 bp on the minus strand; FragGeneScan alone has 49 full-sized genes (368–2,828 bp) that no pyfgs gene overlaps. - The mode matters more than the program: `-w 0` calls about 390 more genes than `-w 1`, and about 880 shared genes have a different start. - None of the 49 FragGeneScan-only genes is behind a `not_called` miss on the complete genome: for 10 of the 15, both callers have a gene there that does not pass the match test (mostly partial or pseudo truth CDS); for the other 5, neither calls one. # New IS-CDS validation independent of gene quality The curated score matches eris's pyfgs genes to RefSeq CDS, so gene-calling errors (a spurious short ORF, a gene that misses the 50% overlap, a CDS pyfgs never called) count against eris. The new **assignment score** asks only: *did eris attach its own genes to the right side of the right IS?* The answer key is built from the truth IS BED and eris's own called genes, and flanks are matched by gene ID, so gene calling cannot cause a mismatch. ## Pipeline ```{=html} ``` 1. **Run eris** on each assembly twice: hops 3 is scored; hops 20 only tells a `budget` miss from `not_reported`. 2. **Place every gene eris called** (CDS and pseudogenes in `_assembly.gff`) on the reference. 3. **Answer key**: for each IS copy in the BED and each side (read along the BED strand), the nearest placed eris gene is *expected*. Tied genes, e.g. identical IS26 transposases, form one relation that any of them finds. 4. **Detected IS**: the new `_loci.fasta` header gives each locus's position (`contig:start-end strand=` or the contig path when stitched). A locus is placed with 1 kb of context to tell identical copies apart; a copy no locus covers is `undetected`. 5. **Score by gene ID**: precision over eris's nearest flanks (FP: `unplaceable`, `overcall`, `wrong_side`, `wrong_IS`, `not_nearest_gene`); recall over expected relations (FN: `undetected`, `wrong_side`, `wrong_IS`, `not_found`). The headline leaves the IS-detection errors (`overcall`, `undetected`) out. ## Results ::: {#be72e531 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} RULES = ["any_copy", "own_copy"] assigned = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f"../result/eris_validation/EC958/{a}/assignment/{r}/metrics.tsv", sep="\t") for a in ASSEMBLIES for r in RULES]) assigned = assigned[assigned["class"] == "both"].rename(columns={"edge_rule": "rule"}) assigned = assigned.set_index(["assembly_type", "rule"])[["precision", "recall", "f1", "overcall", "undetected"]] curated = pd.read_csv("../result/eris_validation/metrics.tsv", sep="\t") curated = curated[(curated["dimension"] == "side") & (curated["class"] == "both")] curated = curated.set_index("assembly_type")[["precision", "recall", "f1"]] curated = curated.reindex(assigned.index.get_level_values(0)).set_axis(assigned.index) table = pd.concat({"Assignment score": assigned, "Curated score": curated}, axis=1).round(3) table = table.reindex(list(ASSEMBLIES), level=0).rename(index=ASSEMBLIES) table.index.names = ["assembly", "rule"] table ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: - Most of what the curated score counts against eris is gene calling: on the complete genome eris's side assignment reaches F1 0.94–0.96 against 0.70. - The 4 `overcall` FPs are two ISEc49 loci with no ISEc49 copy in the BED. - Remaining errors on the complete genome: IS609 flanks on the opposite side to the BED (its family has no inverted repeats, so the orientation may be a convention difference); ISSen10 and ISSen1, short partial copies eris does not detect; and BED `IS26_2` (HG941719.1:37108–38748, 1,640 bp, twice IS26's length), which eris calls ISEcp1. **To check: is this copy really ISEcp1?** ## `any_copy` vs `own_copy` Every IS contains its own transposase, which is never its own flank. The two rules differ only for a gene inside a *neighbouring* IS: `any_copy` leaves out genes inside any IS copy, `own_copy` only those inside the copy being judged. eris itself walks outward and reports every gene it meets, so at two adjacent IS it reports the neighbour's transposase. ```{=html} ``` - This pattern (IS30/IS600, ISEc9/IS5, IS26/ISEcp1) is the whole difference on the complete genome: 16 FP under `any_copy`, 11 under `own_copy`. - Which rule is right is a biology question: should a neighbouring IS's transposase count as "the gene next to this IS"? Decide by reading these rows, not by the higher score.
